name: Remote computers
summary: Lets your agents see and, when you allow it, control other computers over your private Tailscale network, through a MeshCentral server that runs inside this connector. Each agent starts at Look (pictures and facts only); Act and Drive ask for your approval each session unless you turn asking off for that agent.

settings.label: This computer's tailnet name
settings.help: This computer's tailnet name, for example hub.example.ts.net. The remote computers connect to this name, so it must be the one Tailscale shows for this computer.

settings.label: This computer's tailnet address
settings.help: This computer's tailnet address (100.x.y.z). Remote computers reach the server only on this address.

settings.label: Control port
settings.help: Used only on this computer (127.0.0.1) by this connector.

settings.label: Computer port
settings.help: The port on the tailnet address that the remote computers connect to.

settings.label: Addresses the computers may connect from
settings.help: Only computers connecting from these addresses are accepted. IPv4 addresses or ranges (for example 100.64.0.0/10), separated by commas. The default is the whole Tailscale range.

settings.label: What each agent may do
settings.help: Choose each agent's level beside its name. Look = pictures and facts; Act = also run commands; Drive = also click and type. Asking before each session is on by default.

settings.label: Agents that are not asked
settings.help: Agents listed here start an Act or Drive session on a computer without asking you each time, but only up to the level set above; you still get a notice on that computer and every action is logged. Leave empty to be asked for every session.

settings.label: Approved session length (minutes)
settings.help: How long one approval of act or drive lasts.

settings.label: Run as
settings.help: auto, service or hub. On Linux with systemd, MeshCentral runs as its own locked-down system service (service), which you install once with a command that needs an administrator password. hub runs it under My Maestro's own account and is only for computers without systemd. auto picks service when this computer has systemd.

settings.label: Service name
settings.help: The name of the system service and of its account when Run as is service. Leave it as it is unless you need a second copy.
